MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 10, 2017

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:00 p.m., on January 10, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 5, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths (arrived at 5:42 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS

At the hour of 5:00 p.m., Mayor Bucknum declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:00
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Bucknum

City Council Minutes  1  January 10, 2017
 PRESENTATIONS

P1. Opening Remarks from Mayor Bucknum

  Mayor Bucknum discussed her goals for the coming year.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Carole Weidler, M.V.: on behalf of the Marine Adoption Committee, she thanked local businesses,
the Nadadores, the Disney store and especially the giving and generous Mission Viejo residents
for filling toy collection boxes for the City's adopted Marine families. She said that the Marine
Adoption Committee distributed more than 2,500 toys over the holidays and Albertsons market
provided 64 turkey dinners.

Nancy Larkin, M.V.: discussed overcrowding in her neighborhood due to multiple residents in
single family homes and the excess cars parked on the streets as a result.

Gail Reavis, M.V.: stated that the City has spent hundreds of thousands of dollars looking at the
retail center across from city hall and asked the Council to take it a step further and find out if the
tenants are willing to pay more rent if the center is upgraded. She also asked that the City drop its
lawsuit against Cathy Schlicht.

Ryan Burris, M.V.: Chief Communications Officer for Capistrano Unified School District
(CUSD) M.V.: speaking on behalf of the CUSD Board of Trustees and Superintendent, he
congratulated Council Members Kelley and Goodell on their election and affirmed CUSD's
commitment to working with the Council Members and staff in support of the 6,800 children who
attend Mission Viejo schools.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 9 and 11 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

City Council Minutes  2  January 10, 2017
   Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  (1) Approved the Minutes for the special City Council meeting of December 8, 2016, as
  presented, and (2) approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of December
  13, 2016, as presented.

3.  Ordinance Amending Various Sections of Title 10 of the Mission Viejo Municipal
  Codes

  Introduced Ordinance 17-322 Adopting Comprehensive Revisions to Title 10 of the
  Mission Viejo Municipal Code as Set Forth on Attachment B.

4.  Check Register Dated December 2, 2016 in the Amount of $707,476.08

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register Dated December 9, 2016 in the Amount of $662,790.70

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Check Register Dated December 13, 2016 in the Amount of $386,028.47

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

7.  Mileage Reimbursement

  Adopted Resolution 17-01 Adopting the Standard IRS Mileage Reimbursement Rate of
  53.5 Cents Per Mile Effective January 1, 2017.

8.  Quarterly Check Register Report - First Quarter of FY 2016-17

  Received and filed.

10.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - First Quarter of 2016-17

  Received and filed.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

9.  Fiscal Year 2015-16 Mission Viejo Housing Authority Annual Report

City Council Minutes  3  January 10, 2017
   Mayor Pro Tem Sachs asked staff to provide, at the upcoming budget
  workshop, information on the anticipated payments to the City on the $4 million
  promissory note.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to receive
  and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

11.  Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo for the Fiscal
  Year Ended June 30, 2016 and related reports

  Council Member Kelley commended staff for the Comprehensive Annual Financial Report
  (CAFR) and stated that it is an excellent document. She requested that staff provide a brief
  budget overview at the next City Council Meeting and prior to the budget workshop.

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs noted that under financial highlights, the report shows $27.2 million
  in unrestricted net assets. He said that this is the first time since 2012 that reserves have
  been this low and he wants to make sure that the Council is always looking at the net
  reserves number.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to
  receive and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

12.  Marguerite Aquatics Complex Renovation (CIP 14325) - Energy Efficiency
  Improvements

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report
  and answered the City Council Members questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve
  Contract Amendment No 1. to Construct 1 One Corp. in an amount not to exceed $215,170.40

City Council Minutes  4  January 10, 2017
   for Energy Efficient construction items; and (2) adopt Resolution 17-02 Amending CIP 325
  Marguerite Aquatics Complex Budget by $215,170.40 Using Forfeited C and D Deposits.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

13.  Consideration of Expanding the Planning Commission Appointees to Seven (7)
  Members from the Current Five (5)

  City Attorney Curley presented the staff report.

  The following expressed opposition to the proposal to add two members to the Planning and
  Transportation Commission: Gail Reavis, M.V.; Cathy Schlicht, M.V.; and Nancy Larkin,
  M.V.

  The Council Members expressed their opinions about the possibility of expanding the
  Planning and Transportation Commission to seven members and ultimately, there was no
  motion to move forward with the proposal.

14.  Appointment  of  City  Commission
  Members

  Gail Reavis, M.V.: stated that she didn't submit a commission application because she
  knew she wouldn't be appointed.

  The City Council members nominated the following individuals to the City Commissions:

  Community Services Commission
  Council Member Goodell nominated – Victoria Avery
  Council Member Kelley nominated – Cathy Allen
  Council Member Raths nominated – Grant Voss
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs nominated Gary Magill and Robert Ruesch (senior appointment)
  Mayor Bucknum nominated Judy Bullockus and Pam Smith (senior appointment)

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Raths, to ratify
  the seven nominations to the Community Services Commission.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
City Council Minutes  5  January 10, 2017
   Investment Advisory Commission
  Council Member Goodell nominated – Nina Altountash
  Council Member Kelley nominated – Steve Spillman
  Council Member Raths nominated – Dennis (Scott) McClellan
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs nominated – Kathy Miramontes
  Mayor Bucknum nominated – Richard Steinhoff

  Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to ratify the
  five nominations to the Investment Advisory Commission.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Planning and Transportation Commission
  Council Member Goodell nominated – Joseph C. Blum
  Council Member Kelley nominated – Robert D. Breton
  Council Member Raths nominated – Dave Leckness
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs nominated – David Mandsdoerfer
  Mayor Bucknum nominated – Julia Malisos

  Motion made by Council Member Raths, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to ratify
  the five nominations to the Planning and Transportation Commission.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

15.  City Council Committee and Regional Board/Committee  Representative
  Appointments and Update Posting of FPPC Form 806 Online

  Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to appoint Mayor
  Pro Tem Ed Sachs as the City's representative on the Orange County Fire Authority Board
  of Directors.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  Sachs

  Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to appoint Mayor
  Pro Tem Ed Sachs as the City's representative on the Transportation Corridor Agencies
  Board of Directors.
City Council Minutes  6  January 10, 2017
   AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  Sachs

  Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Raths, to appoint
  Council Member Trish Kelley as the City's alternate on the Transportation Corridor
  Agencies Board of Directors.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  Kelley

  Mayor Bucknum appointed members to the existing City of Mission Viejo Committees
  (direct appointments by the Mayor, no vote required):

  (a) CUSD Ad Hoc Committee: Wendy Bucknum and Trish Kelley

  (b) Standing Economic Development Committee: Brian Goodell and Ed Sachs

  (c) Marguerite Aquatics Complex Oversight Ad Hoc Committee: Wendy Bucknum
  and Greg Raths

  (d) Confirming Interim Zoning Ordinance Ad Hoc Committee: Brian Goodell and
  Ed Sachs

  Mayor Bucknum appointed representatives and alternates to the following regional
  boards/committees (direct appointments by the Mayor, no vote required):

  (a) California Joint Powers Insurance Authority: Trish Kelley and Cheryl Dyas

  (b) League of California Cities and Association of California Cities, Orange
  County: Wendy Bucknum and Ed Sachs

  (c) Orange County Council of Governments General Assembly: Brian Goodell and
  Trish Kelley

  (d) Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) General Assembly:
  Wendy Bucknum and Trish Kelley

  (e) Southern Orange County Watershed Management Area Executive Committee –
  Trish Kelley and Brian Goodell

City Council Minutes  7  January 10, 2017
   (f) Oversight Board (by adoption of Resolution 17-03 required/attached) – Robert
  Breton and Cheryl Dyas

  By consensus, the City Council directed the City Clerk to update the appointees list as
  required by law on Form 806 and post that form to the City's website.

STAFF REPORTS

16.  Presentation on Lake Loop Connectivity Plan

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented a report on the
  proposed Lake Loop Connectivity Plan.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

17.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell expressed his appreciation for the support he has received from his
colleagues and the community. He stated that he kind of expected to be attacked, as he was tonight,
for the monetary support he received during his election campaign. He noted that his main
supporter is someone who simply believes in him but has no interest in the community. Council
Member Goodell welcomed his former swim coach, Mark Shubert, who has returned to the
Nadadores as the Associate Coach and he stated that he looks forward to great things ahead for the
Nadadores teams and the newly refurbished aquatics facility. In closing, Council Member Goodell
announced that he will be attending a League of California Cities workshop for new Council
Members and he looks forward to learning how to be even more effective as a Council Member in
serving the citizens of Mission Viejo.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley asked that former Planning and Transportation Commissioner Steve
Spillman be invited to a future Council Meeting to share some conceptual plans that he created to
enhance Oso Creek. She also reiterated her request to staff for a budget overview, prior to the
budget workshop. Council Member Kelley thanked those who applied for appointment to a
Commission and asked the unsuccessful applicants to look for other opportunities to serve the
City. She thanked community members for their generosity in donating to the Marine Adoption
Committee’s toy drive and discussed the overwhelming response. In closing, Council Member
Kelley announced that the Community of Character word for the month of January is perseverance

City Council Minutes  8  January 10, 2017
 and the character movie is The Rosa Parks Story, which will be shown in the Council chamber on
Sunday, January 15, 2017, at 2:00 p.m.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths asked if staff could brief the Council on ridership of the Mission Viejo
shuttle at the next City Council Meeting. He also recognized several residents in the audience and
thanked them for attending the Council meeting.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs thanked Council Member Raths for his time and participation on the
Economic Development Committee over the last two years. He expressed concern with cyber
security and stated that the City needs to continue to pay attention to that. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
announced that during the budget workshop, he is going to request that some money is allocated
to do department audits as well as procurement and vendor audits. He also asked Lieutenant
Binning about the double-double lines in the freeway carpool lanes that used to be yellow but were
recently painted white. Lt. Binning responded that the State of California chose to paint all the
double-double lines white to conform with new federal standards. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs shared
that he is closely following pension liability issues in the state and he noted the trend to slowly
reduce the discount rate so there is no big impact to municipalities. In closing, Mayor Pro Tem
Sachs stated that he is looking forward to working with his colleagues as everyone on the Council
wants to do good work for the City. He feels that they are committed to making sure that taxpayer
money is not spent on foolish things and all of the Council Members consider public safety to be
the number one factor.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum asked the Chief of Police Services and the Fire Authority’s Division Chief to
provide regular updates on their respective departments at the City Council Meetings. She talked
about longtime Mission Viejo resident and the co-owner of Accell Property Management, Steven
Kent Feistel, who recently passed away and announced that she will be adjourning the meeting in
his name.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:17 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting in memory of resident Steve Feistel, to Tuesday, January
24, 2017, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of January 24, 2017
City Council Minutes  9  January 10, 2017
